test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I don’t think your sister is enjoying the party. She ______ at her watch for the last half an hour.
solution:
The correct answer is- 'has been looking.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In the given sentence the verb '*has been looking*' is the correct choice to fill.
 
• The preceding sentence in the **present continuous tense** suggests that the party is **still **going on.
 
• So, to show an action started in the *past *and is continuing at the *present *time, we use the **present perfect continuous **tense.
 
 
• **Example**: *I have been reading War and Peace for a month now.*
 
 
 
• Thus *option 4 *is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: *I don’t think your sister is enjoying the party. She **has been looking** at her watch for the last half an hour.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn about the **present perfect continuous tense**:

 
 
• **Recently **and **lately **are words that we often find with **verbs **in the *present perfect continuous tense*. 

 
 
• Example: 

 
 
• *I haven’t been feeling well **lately**. (*To convey that *I am still not feeling well)*
 
 
 
 
 
• ​​Not all verbs are **compatible **with *continuous action*. In this case, the sentence structure is different:
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​I have been owning this house since 2007.* (**incorrect**)
 
• *I have owned this house since 2007. *(**correct**)
 
 
 
 
 
 

b0:T
